claims.text: The proposed approach will decouple lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Machine-learning-augmented ab initio calculations can explicitly model anharmonic lattice dynamics for HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed method will accurately predict the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The method will outperform Debye-temperature-based and average-force-constant models.
The target samples are defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr, including a variant containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen corresponding to the high-temperature conductivity experiments.
Machine-learning-corrected interatomic force fields will calculate temperature-dependent phonon lifetimes and scattering rates.
Prior total-conductivity measurements are available for HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The relevant atomic-scale mediator is anharmonic lattice distortion and force-constant fluctuation caused by high chemical disorder.
Explicit phonon simulation captures complex mass and force-constant variations beyond an average Debye-temperature approximation.
Combining machine learning with ab initio lattice dynamics permits independent prediction of lattice and electronic thermal transport.
Predicted lattice thermal conductivity will agree with experimentally separated lattice contributions to within 10–20%.
The new method will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 30% relative to earlier analytical or Debye-based models.
Independently estimated electronic contributions will align with HfNbTaTiZr transport measurements below 200 K.
Earlier analytical and DFT-derived estimates conflate lattice and electronic contributions and have lattice-conductivity uncertainties exceeding 30–40%.
The method is primarily reliable from 300 to 1200 K for near-ideal, defect-free samples and is less reliable below 200 K.
Samples with substantially higher oxygen or defect concentrations fall outside the proposed predictive domain.
A deviation greater than ±20% between predicted and experimentally separated lattice thermal conductivity over 300–1200 K, or failure of the predicted channel separation, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The samples are repeatedly described as defect-free or near-ideal while one required variant contains approximately 1 wt.% interstitial oxygen and the conditions simultaneously call this controlled oxygen contamination. An oxygen-doped specimen is not literally defect-free.
